outcome.technical: RULE 1 (a module that did not load is no case). _runner_output.py: unittest case records keep their printed location as `where`, pytest records their `kind`; new `did_not_load(failure)` is the one test of which a failure is (unittest's `unittest.loader._FailedTest` stand-in, in the 3.8-3.10 and 3.11+ spellings, and a pytest `ERROR <file>` node with no `::`); new public reader `load_failures(text, runner=None)` names each such module with the runner's own line (unittest's `Failed to import test module` line joined with the cause its traceback ends on; pytest's `E` gutter line, never its `Hint:`). stamp-verification.py: `_loaded_split` (the one caller of did_not_load) is read by BOTH verdicts. green_verdict asks it after the baseline and inline checks and BEFORE `_not_green_failure`: any load failure is `could-not-prove` (verdict collection-error) with the runner's line, whether or not other cases ran. red_verdict removes load failures from its failing list and names them apart in every basis after that point (prefixed onto env_clause); its verdicts and statuses are unchanged, since a load failure never failed an assertion and was never credited. Where red and green read the same output differently: a run holding one module that did not load beside an own case failing an assertion is still `proved` by red (a located own assertion failed) and `could-not-prove` by green (it cannot say the task's tests pass on the base); an ImportError of a name the task introduces is proved by red through its --introduces second run and is could-not-prove for green. A module-level RuntimeError under a NAMED unittest module crashes with no tally (unittest does not catch it) and was already could-not-prove (no-tally), the RuntimeError line in the basis. RULE 2 (a rising count proves only what the task defines). The red verb's definition reading is factored so both verbs share it: `_definition_in(tree, classes, name)` (what `_definition` now calls), `_head_copy(classes, name, node, defs)` (credit_problem's HEAD-identical test) and `_js_head_copy(chain, bodies, head)` (_js_credit_problem's); red's messages are byte-identical. New `own_definitions(texts, runner, head_defs, head_js)` (with `_case_defs`, `_py_own`, `_js_own`, `_one_case`) counts the cases the declared test files define - the def that runs, `test`-prefixed, a top-level class's method for unittest, also module-level and nested for pytest; jest/vitest/playwright title chains - that HEAD's test files do not hold identically, and lists what it cannot count (a decorator that may generate cases such as parametrize - unittest skip family, expectedFailure, mock.patch and pytest.mark.* other than parametrize count as one case; load_tests / pytest_generate_tests; a JS title built at run time; an unparsed file; HEAD unread). `_count_proof` replaces the bare count route of `_own_passing`: N own definitions, M = cases skipped or expected to fail beyond HEAD's own run; proved only when N > M (basis: `N defined > M more skipped, so at least one of the task's own ran and passed`); otherwise could-not-prove, `(0 defined)` -> `the rise is made of cases HEAD already holds`, `(N defined, M more skipped)` -> `... or of cases that did not run`. RULE 3: with no texts in ctx, or a runner the reading does not know, the count proves as before with `(the declared test files' definitions were not read, so the rise is not shown to be cases the task defines)`; with uncounted definitions and N <= M it proves as `a weaker proof than a count of them`, never a refusal. House runs and sweep-shaped commands are untouched (their own id and per-file routes; go8 guards it). run_green gathers `head_tree` (the same reader red uses) and the declared files' texts less the support modules run at HEAD's copy, into ctx keys `wt`, `head_defs`, `head_js`. What it answers for: an inherited-class file with one own passing case -> proved (go3, go9 `inherits`); a parametrised or generated case -> weaker proof, labelled (go7); a new case in an existing file -> proved (go3); house and sweep -> unchanged (go8, existing gf1/gf5/gf8/gf13 green). Known limits, stated in the docstrings: N counts every declared file's own definitions whether or not the command reached that file, and a case built by setattr or type() has no def and is not seen (a file holding only such cases is refused with `0 defined`). An un-skipped HEAD case counts as own (its decorator list changed, so its ast differs), so the reviewer's low U11 still reads proved.
